Plan additive arm and waist effort without robot I/O.

A native-MC-owned receiver is required before this can be applied
while standing; direct HAL publishing would compete with balance.

Return the native impedance integration contract without I/O.

Frame preparation and reply validation are available. A native MC
receiver is not implemented; submit() refuses physical execution.

Calculate an offline, compensation-aware transition after arrival.

This performs no I/O, even when dry_run=False. It cannot enable the
native hold backend or qualify a physical gain transition.

Analyze supplied arm-hold evidence without connecting or commanding.

Pose readiness is separate from command compensation and native
transition qualification. This method never enables physical holding.

Report native golf-hold capability without sending robot commands.

The installed native custom-preset handoff is unqualified at arbitrary
poses. The returned session reports unsupported for both live and dry
runs. It cannot move the waist or restore gains in place.
Return selected saved telemetry columns; never connects to Master.
Return all saved session data as readable, iterable tables.

Enter the selected current-hold guidance owner.

``right`` preserves the established right-only route. ``both`` selects
the qualified bilateral route. Those are the only public choices.

Accept an explicitly chosen stationary hold after a tracking fault.

Preserves commands and native ownership. This does not clear watchdog,
hardware, freshness, or command-domain faults and never moves the robot.

App-compatible explicit arm-owner release; waist stays unverified.

Requires a completed stationary arm return in native STAND_DEFAULT.
Never replays a return, changes waist targets, or restores stiffness.
A failed acknowledgement is observed once, never resent.
Alias for the app's release_returned_hold().

Return the guided arms and waist together, then release the hold.

Absolute targets do not depend on which joints were adjusted or on
adjustment history. Bilateral guidance restores both arms, even when
only one arm or only the waist moved. Right-only guidance retains its
original side contract. The existing arm return starts at the native
waist return boundary, not after the waist completes. An already-neutral
waist does not prevent the arm return. Native balance and waist gains
stay unchanged; real standing stiffness is a separate operation.

An internal duration selects a shared nominal motion window; actual
arrival and settling must still be measured. Release only follows
verified returns, never elapsed time or reversal of adjustment history.

Restore only the real standing arm stiffness, never the body pose.

Call restore_stand_hand_guide() separately when a position return is
wanted. This function must not launch an arm/waist return, replay undo,
or use Heart as a fallback. Its native handoff checks the existing pose
and ownership before proceeding; it never corrects them implicitly.
Startup gains and settled final feedback, not the raw STAND_DEFAULT
label or service acceptance, determine success. transitionVerified
covers arm/head command targets and retained native balance/ownership.
The waist's native HAL servo output is reported separately: it is not
the requested body target. This receipt does not claim physical waist
smoothness; that requires the separately recorded physical observation.

Select arm stiffness without requesting a Heart pose or body mode change.

Hard uses Heart preset gains at the admitted golf hold. Medium delegates
restore_stand_default, retaining its default-pose and ownership checks.
Its native profile currently equals the Heart gains. Soft returns both
arms and waist through restore_stand_hand_guide (12/1.5, not zero torque).

For hard, the arm movement must already be complete; it does not
move the waist or start a new arm trajectory. A live hard handoff requires
the current bilateral golf owner, explicit test-stand confirmation,
native STAND_DEFAULT balance, and the complete telemetry gate.  When
the robot is already in the native high-gain golf hold, the same call
is idempotent and performs a three-second read-only verification.

Run the saved setup, hard hold, backswing and +5 N.m forward stroke.

In live mode, invoking this preset is the operator's acknowledgement
that the robot is supported, supervised and its swing area is clear.
Native capability, ownership, telemetry and endpoint admission still
run inside ``golf_put``. Dry-run mode only returns the full plan.
Ends in the final powered hold; restoration is a separate call.

Establish the saved firm arm hold, then bend the waist and swing.

Each stage uses its existing owner and endpoint checks. A partial or
uncertain result stops the sequence without an automatic retry or
return; the last powered controller remains responsible for the pose.

Run saved bilateral Movement B with explicit duration-based stages.

The requested rate is a ceiling, not guaranteed measured speed. Existing
derivative envelopes can lower it. Requires a healthy bilateral owner;
never starts/restarts a controller, resets faults, or restores a pose.

Close a door with one arm followed by a waist turn.

``right`` moves the right arm and turns the waist left; ``left`` mirrors
that action. The elbow and shoulder pitch move in one arm request. The
waist request starts only after that arm request reaches a stationary
powered hold. Per-joint timing uses the measured response model so the
two arm joints finish together.

Copy a fresh arm pose to its opposite using the normal absolute API.

This is one captured pose, not continuous following or a recording replay.
All seven target axes share one governed request. No controller is started,
no fault is cleared, and failed or uncertain requests are never resent.

Move both arms together to one mirrored SDK pose.

All fourteen joints use a single bilateral request and common clock.
At most two additional correction rounds address observed load shifts
after completed stages. Failed or uncertain requests are never resent.
Hardware timing and full-pose precision are reported, not assumed.

Enter the qualified product-presentation pose, right arm first.

Starts bilateral guided control from verified normal standing when
needed. The recorded pickup flows into the center transition; final
presentation needs an SDK-confirmed stationary powered hold. Bounded
endpoint-precision warnings remain visible in the result. Leaves
the presentation pose powered; never restores or retries on failure.
Product overlays and their camera calibration belong to the scene app.

Move both elbows to one absolute bend angle in one shared request.

Example: Agentech.move_elbows_to(90). Other arm axes hold their current
commands. Uses move_arms_to validation and measured endpoint checks;
does not issue sequential left/right adjustments or retry failures.

Move selected arm joints to absolute signed SDK angles in degrees.

Example: move_arms_to(left={"elbow": 50}, right={"elbow": 50}).
Each arm may select all three shoulder axes, its elbow, and all three wrist
axes in one shared trajectory. Omitted joints retain their commands.
Explicit zero is a target, not an omitted axis. Elbow positive means
bend; shoulder/wrist signs follow the existing SDK joint coordinates.
